sections.heading: Why Functioning Door Closers Matter for Commercial Properties
sections.body: Door closers are one of the most mechanically active components on any commercial entrance. Every time a door opens, the closer absorbs force, controls swing speed, and guides the door back to a fully latched position. Over time, hydraulic fluid can leak, pivot arms wear down, springs lose tension, and adjustment screws slip out of calibration. When any of these failures occur, the consequences range from doors that slam shut and startle occupants to doors that fail to latch and leave your building unsecured. For property managers and facility directors in McLean, a malfunctioning door closer is more than an inconvenience — it is a liability. Tenants notice, visitors notice, and the repeated stress of an improperly closing door accelerates damage to the frame, hinges, and glass. Addressing closer problems promptly preserves the full hardware assembly and avoids the higher cost of a full door replacement later. Our technicians understand the demands placed on commercial entrance hardware and approach every repair with the thoroughness your property deserves.

sections.heading: Common Door Closer Problems We Repair in McLean
sections.body: Our service calls in the McLean area cover a wide range of door closer issues, and most can be resolved without replacing the entire unit. Hydraulic leaks are among the most frequent problems we encounter — when the fluid that controls closing speed escapes the cylinder, the door either slams or drifts without closing fully. We inspect the body, seals, and valves to determine whether resealing or full unit replacement is the right approach. Misadjusted closing and latching speeds are another common complaint, particularly in high-traffic buildings near the McLean Metro Station or along Old Dominion Drive where doors open and close dozens of times each day. We recalibrate sweep speed, latch speed, and back-check settings to match your door weight and traffic volume. Bent or broken arm assemblies, stripped mounting hardware, and cracked closer bodies are also routine repairs we handle efficiently. Our technicians carry a broad inventory of components compatible with leading commercial closer brands so most jobs are completed in a single visit.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Replacement Door Closer
sections.body: When a door closer is beyond economical repair, selecting the right replacement unit is critical to long-term performance. Commercial door closers vary significantly by door weight, frame configuration, application type, and mounting method. A surface-mounted closer suitable for an interior office door is not the same as a heavy-duty unit designed for a high-frequency exterior entrance. Parallel arm, top jamb, and regular arm mounting configurations each serve different frame conditions, and choosing the wrong one creates immediate installation problems or premature failure. Our technicians evaluate your door size, weight, swing direction, and usage patterns before recommending a replacement. We supply and install commercial-grade closers built for durability in demanding environments, ensuring the unit we install is matched to your actual conditions rather than a generic default. We also take time to calibrate the new closer precisely so it performs correctly from day one, protecting both the hardware and the surrounding door frame from unnecessary stress.

faq.q: How do I know if my commercial door closer needs repair or full replacement?
faq.a: In many cases, door closers can be repaired rather than replaced. If the unit is leaking hydraulic fluid, moving sluggishly, or failing to latch, a technician can often recalibrate settings, reseal the body, or replace worn components to restore function. Full replacement is typically recommended when the closer body is cracked, the internal mechanism is seized, or the unit is so old that compatible parts are no longer available. Our technicians assess each closer on-site and give you an honest recommendation based on the condition and cost-effectiveness of repair versus replacement.

faq.q: How long does a commercial door closer repair typically take?
faq.a: Most commercial door closer repairs in McLean are completed within one to two hours. Straightforward recalibration or minor adjustments take less time, while repairs involving hydraulic resealing or arm assembly replacement may take a bit longer. Full unit replacements, including removal of the old closer and precise installation and calibration of the new one, are typically finished within a single service visit. We come prepared with common replacement parts and hardware so delays caused by missing components are minimized.
